column2: End-of-year student evaluation meeting (Zeuch, Mangold, Gair, Schawinsky, Evarts, Weston, Albers, Wunsch, Steinau, King, Dreier, French, Rice): the cases of “Cane,” “Carter,” “Norris”…
Continuation of the end-of-year student evaluations
Board meeting: Goldenson allowed to resign (a “goofy resolution,” according to Mangold)
Mangold to Adamic on the Huxley-Heard visit (“talking to Huxley over transatlantic telephone”)
Board meeting on the purchase of Lake Eden (then June 5, 1937)

Last general meeting of the year (five hours): Beverly Coleman reads the 24-point critique by eight departing students (Alsberg, Coleman, Harrington…), “I AM GOD complex”; Georgia's salary cut is revealed; Zeuch, ill in bed, is summoned; Portell-Vila angrily walks out with his wife; Georgia leaves, slamming the door three times; Rice turns the meeting around
Board meeting at the start of the summer move-out: Portell-Vila's resignation submitted, then withdrawn after a talk with Rice; Georgia's resignation accepted with the equivalent of a year's salary
Legal settlement between Georgia and the college: $3,500 (two payments of $250, six of $500, without interest)
Rice to Henry Allen Moe: Portell, “a more disgraceful exhibition”; Georgia's savings
Mangold to David Bailey on the June 1 meeting
Rice to Adamic on Georgia
Moe to Rice (on the Cubans and autonomy)
Mangold to Martin: the meeting was “the tensest thing that has ever happened around here”
Evarts to Mangold: “bluntness has its limits”
Tasker Howard to Mangold: “a dismal display”; he knows “what war feels like”
A. Lawrence Kocher to Dreier (building plans)
Mangold to Brenda Gair: Alice “damn good”; minor frictions
Albers to Rice (hostility; they now communicate only by notes in the mailboxes)
Meeting of almost the whole faculty on Rice's situation: all except Portell and Dreier want to support him
Rice decides to go away to rest for three or four weeks
Rice-Mangold-Dreier talk, reported to the faculty the same day: a “leave of absence” for Rice until May 1; Alice will not be penalized
Rice to Adamic: “panic and almost lunacy”; a sense of betrayal
Rice drives alone to Folly Beach (South Carolina), to a borrowed cottage; Nell Rice goes to her brother's in Swarthmore
Mangold to Adamic on Rice's absence
Suicide of the student Dick Porter (a bullet to the temple one afternoon); Moellenhoff and Dr. Richardson take him to the Biltmore hospital in Asheville, where he dies on the operating table
General meeting the morning after the suicide: Fritz Moellenhoff speaks on “self-chosen” loneliness
Morton Steinau to Mrs. Porter (then May 6, 1938)
Mangold to Betty Young (then April 5)
Mangold visits Rice at Folly Beach
Mangold to Rice on the hostility toward Schawinsky
Rice asks the faculty's opinion on his return in May
Special meeting of the Board: Rice's leave unanimously extended until September, $100 paid toward his expenses
Four faculty members visit Rice at Folly Beach; he reproaches them for thinking only of the college
Morton Steinau to Mrs. Porter
Special meeting of the Board: another $200 for Rice, invited to represent the college at a meeting of progressive schools in Chicago (he declines)
Confidential memo to the Board: Schawinsky will not be rehired; he leaves for the New Bauhaus in Chicago
Mangold to Wunsch: Rice “a fine actor” toward Dreier
Dreier's telegram inviting Eleanor Roosevelt
Tasker Howard to Mangold (then Mangold's reply on January 18: Rice-Dreier-Albers relations “workable”)
Faculty meeting: Gropius and Breuer commissioned to design a central complex (fee $400)
Board meeting: sabbatical leave for Rice in 1939-40 (autobiography)
Time on the Gropius-Breuer plans for Black Mountain
Dreier to Mangold: the Gropius-Breuer project would cost $500,000
“J. A. Rice finally got the hell out of here this morning”; Nell refuses to live near him
Board meeting (the Rice question)
Dreier to Steinau: the draft signed by Rice “comes pretty close to being dishonest” (a $145 car repair)
Wunsch's first visit to Rice in Southern Pines to obtain his resignation (a game of cat and mouse)
New York Herald Tribune: Gropius's speech on his plans for BMC
Wunsch to Rice (“calm, friendly, and wise”) and to “Jack”: the Board can no longer gamble on Rice
Wunsch's second visit, with Nell Rice, to Southern Pines: Rice refuses to resign (“I want to redeem myself”); Nell refuses to live with him again
The Board waits a week, then formally asks for Rice's resignation
Rice resigns by return mail; the letter is shown to the faculty and the student officers
Wunsch's third visit (with Nell) to Southern Pines: a “tirade,” then cocktails and steak; financial settlement (part of his salary to the end of the year, an allowance, his daughter's education)
Rice's elegiac letter to Wunsch (“the second Old Fashioned”)
Clara McGraw's seven-page report on fund-raising
Newsweek (p. 43) on Rice's resignation
Faculty meeting (the move, financing; then May 8, 1940)
Statement by Rector Wunsch to the community on the departure of three students in 1939-40 (suspension by the Discipline Committee, illness, drunkenness with a weapon)
Faculty meeting: the Gropius-Breuer plans abandoned; decision to move to Lake Eden
Board meeting: the five-year lease with the Blue Ridge Assembly expires in June 1941 (Dr. Weatherford plans a girls' school in Lee Hall)
K. Katz to Mangold on Richard Gothe
Dreier to A. Lawrence Kocher (July 8, 11, 17): commission for a single “Studies Building”
Dreier to Forbes (Gothe; purchase of Lake Eden)
Kocher to Dreier and Albers (wood or stone for the Studies Building)
New York Herald Tribune on the construction
Asheville Citizen-Times: photographs and an article on the construction (Claude Stoller: “a new electric train at Christmas”)
Frances de Graaff to Wunsch (application)
PM’s Weekly on Black Mountain
Wunsch to Mangold on Gothe's “arrogance”
Mangold to Forbes on former students
Wunsch to Mangold on Rice's bitter loneliness
Betty Brett's diary: her first day as crew leader (a firebreak ditch with Kurtz and Kaye)
The faculty sets the “optimal” time for construction work at one to three afternoons a week
Official opening of the college at Lake Eden (breakfasts in overcoats in unfinished buildings)
Dreier to the trustees of the Whitney Foundation
Pearl Harbor: for the first time since the Willkie campaign, a radio at dinner
General meeting on the students and military service (seven-page minutes)

Just before Christmas 1941: the whole college suspends classes to finish the roof framing of the Studies Building; Richard Carpenter, a biologist afraid of heights, hammers nails all day; a small tree on the ridge, wine and speeches
Dreier to Marshall Field (an offer of $10,000 refused by a faculty member; then July 24, 1943)
Bentley to Wunsch (application; then to Mangold on May 25, Mangold's reply on May 28, 1942)
Mangold to Arthur Adams on accreditation
Letter to the National Selective Service Board to spare the older faculty members; Major T. Upton's reply to Wunsch on May 14
Wunsch visits M. C. Huntley (Southern Association of Colleges): BMC could have applied for the right to grant degrees when it was founded
Robert Dudley French (Jonathan Edwards College, Yale) to Mangold: Bentley “a stormy petrel”
Mangold to Arthur Adams: $76,000 in gifts in 1941-42 (previous record $15,467 in 1937-38), assets estimated at $150,000; salaries paid at 40 % in 1940-41 and 32 % in 1941-42
Letter to Dreier on Fritz Hansgirg (release by the Department of Justice)
Mangold to Ruth O’Neill: review of funding (Carnegie $5,000, Oberlaender $2,700, Whitney $9,000…)
Wunsch to Fred Mangold, shortly after his first meeting with Bentley: “I did not like Bentley”
Letter to Dr. and Mrs. Babbott (fund-raising)
Telegram from Fortune magazine (questionnaire on the effects of the war)
Wunsch to Forbes: the “good things” go on (dancing, rehearsals, Saturday concerts attended by wounded men from Moore General Hospital)
BMC Community Bulletin No. 8 (race relations; also Nos. 14 and 16: Jan. 18 and Feb. 1, 1943)
The Board of Fellows telegraphs the governor of North Carolina against the death sentence of William Wellman, a Black man convicted on flimsy evidence
New Year's Eve party in the South Lodge hall: Wunsch “deeply distressed” (“too much wine”)
Wunsch to Evarts (then February 8, 1943)
Evarts to Wunsch on the refusal to read the autobiography (“Drama, drama, drama”)
Faculty meeting: grading by “outside standards,” additional examinations
Dreier to Forbes: thanks for $3,000; staff layoffs
Serge Chermayeff to Albers (then April 10, 1943): Bertrand Russell might be interested in a full-time position
Wunsch replies to Chermayeff (then April 26, 1943) in negative terms (a “primitive” life; Russell should first come and be looked over)
